title: SAML NameID format mismatch causing role mapping drop and audit suppression in Private clusters
creator: Priya Shah
description: Several enterprise customers on Private (VPC) deployments reported sudden authorization failures and missing audit entries after a routine IdP metadata refresh. Requests that previously mapped to 'admin' and 'devops' roles were being assigned only baseline roles; corresponding audit events for role-change and session invalidation were not being emitted in the control plane, causing support escalation. Impact surfaced across multiple private clusters in different regions.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure Private cluster with SAML IdP using NameID-format urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress
2) Trigger IdP metadata refresh or rotate signing certs on IdP side
3) Perform SSO login for a user with role claims, observe session creation and role assignment in /auth/session endpoint
4) Observe RBAC lookup returning fallback role and absence of role-mapping audit event in control plane audit stream
root_cause: NameID values emitted by a subset of customer IdPs switched from emailAddress to transient persistent formats (NameID format mismatch). Our SAML assertion parser prioritized NameID over the attributes map for role resolution. When NameID did not match expected pattern, role-map lookup short-circuited and audit hook that fires after successful role resolution was skipped. In addition, an optimization in the private control-plane aggregator batched and dropped certain low-priority audit events during short-lived caching pressure introduced during metadata refreshes.
mitigation: 1) Roll out a hotfix to SAML assertion parsing to fall back to attributes.role list when NameID does not match expected patterns. 2) Patch the audit aggregator to persist crucial authz/audit events during IdP metadata refreshes (deprioritize batching for auth events). 3) Temporary customer mitigation: advise affected customers to revert to previous stable IdP metadata or enable attribute-based role assertions on the IdP.
